subject: hoverPickup
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: militarized pickup converted to hover thrusters.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk.
reasoning:
I'm planning a single TypeScript module for a static vehicle model—a pickup truck roughly 5.2m long and 2m wide, with no joints needed since it's not a creature. I need to make sure the lowest points of the geometry touch the ground plane at y=0.

Working out the hull silhouette as a 2D profile (z,y coordinates) to extrude into 3D: lower body slab, hood, windshield slope, roof, and bed walls, all facing +Z with the thruster pods hanging at the corners so their bottoms rest on the floor.

Still writing the body profile points...

I'll separate the cab into its own extrusion since the roof needs to be narrower than the body, then settle on a paint scheme -- going with a dark gunmetal cyberpunk military look, olive-dark base with patch camo and neon magenta/cyan glow accents.

Now I'm planning the decals and textures: svg designs for the windshield with glints, headlights, a unit emblem stencil on the door, hazard stripes, license number, and a hologram HUD element, placed as textured planes facing outward. For the thrusters, I'm positioning four pods at the corners with lathe-built nacelle housings and glowing ring discs underneath.

Working out thruster pod geometry and struts...

I'm also planning the militarized details: a roof turret with clustered minigun barrels, a light bar, antenna, armor plates, bullbar with grille and glowing headlights/taillights, neon underglow strips, armor skirts, and a missile pod on the bed rack. I'm setting up reusable helper functions for boxes and cylinders to keep the part placement code concise, including mirroring symmetric pieces.

Now I'm working out the paint and panel textures for the hull—olive patches with subtle gap lines, pulling in panelled and glow effects from the clockwork kit—plus planning a stenciled door marking texture ("HV-7" with a star and chevrons) positioned on each side of the cab.

For the windshield I'm figuring out placement as a tilted plane running from the lower cab up to the roofline, with a forward-up facing normal, plus adding dark glossy inset planes for the side windows.

Still computing cab geometry...

I'm tilting that plate slightly downward toward the front with a small rotation around the x-axis to match the hood slope, then shifting focus to the body extrusion, making sure the cab area's top profile transitions smoothly between the hood height and the cab roofline.

Now I'm sketching the body outline connecting hood, cab, and bed sections, then adding the bed structure: a floor, side rail walls, a tailgate, and a front wall tucked behind the cab. With the bed in place, I'm starting on the turret, placing a pedestal cylinder as its base in the rear bed area before building out the ring and gun body.

Thinking through the turret's gun housing and barrel placement, I'm checking heights so the barrels clear the cab roof rather than clipping through it, positioning the housing box and five cylindrical barrels angled just above the roofline.

Now I'm adding roof details like light bar boxes with emissive red/blue strips, antennas, a sensor dome, and roof rack rails, then moving to the front end with a bullbar/bumper box, a grille plane with texture, and glowing headlight boxes positioned on the front face.

Taillights go on the tailgate as red glow strips, plus cyan neon strips running along the underside of the hull on both sides, and I'm working out side armor skirts and fender flare panels to add bulk to the body.

Now I'm positioning the pods and figuring out how struts connect them to the body, with diagonal bracing for support, and sketching the lathe profile for the pod shape itself.

Adding fan blades inside the hub with a glowing magenta rim torus, plus vertical side fins, then sketching a thin amber hazard-stripe ring around the pod's midsection.

Now I'm adding rear-mounted thruster exhausts near the base, a dark underbelly skid plate with a glowing cyan lift-core strip down the center, and small cab details like mirrors, door seams, and handles for extra realism.

I'm figuring out door seam placement avoiding the window region, then working out where to put the emblem decal given the cab/body geometry—since the vertical visible area is small, I'll place it on the side armor panel or body flank instead.

Actually I'll skip the armor panel and put the decal directly on the body side with a stencil label, add hazard stripes on the bed, and place another decal on the hood tilted upward with a chevron emblem. I'll skip the tailgate decal, and note that glow strips need flat color rather than paint material.

I'm mapping out the texture list I need: windshield, side windows, grille, flank stencil, hood emblem, and hazard strip, plus the thruster ring—about six total, keeping the SVGs small. For the paint, I'll nest a panelled camo pattern using a seeded patches function with a base color string.

Now I'm defining helper functions for building box and cylinder geometry parts with position, direction, and flat-shading options...

For static parts without joints, I'm confirming boxes can be placed directly without bones. I'm also building a decal helper for planes that applies a texture with position and direction, plus an "up" option for orientation.

Writing thruster assembly code...

Now I'm planning out the remaining details to reach roughly 150 parts total—exhaust, roof accessories, mirrors, wipers, bumper, tow hooks, headlight bezels, spare tire, ammo crates, a missile pod, and an antenna with a glowing tip.

Adjusting the missile pod's size and position so it fits within the bed without overlapping the tailgate, then adding a grid of dark cylinder missile tubes on its front face with glowing red tips.

Setting default export now and finishing up the component.
